data.name: Bayanth
data.gender_notes: Bayanth is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘बायंत’ (Vayant), which means 'Lord of Strength'. In Hindu mythology, Bayanth is a name given to various deities, including Lord Shiva and Vayu, the god of wind. The name Bayanth carries the meaning “Lord of Strength” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bayanth usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Bayanth belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Strength.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bayanth total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bayanth holds significant cultural importance in Hindu society. In Hindu mythology, it is used to refer to powerful deities associated with strength and power. For instance, Lord Shiva, known as the destroyer, and Vayu, the god of wind, are both associated with the name Bayanth. Users of this name may be inspired by the spirit of strength and power associated with these deities.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Bayanth carries deep significance for those who follow Hinduism. It is a reminder of the inner strength and power that lies within each individual. Just as Lord Shiva and Vayu possess immense power, each person has the ability to tap into their own inner strength and overcome challenges. The name Bayanth can serve as a source of inspiration and motivation, reminding individuals to strive for excellence and persevere through adversity. It is a name deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality and serves as a constant reminder of the power within.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bayanth is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vayu', meaning wind or breath of life. The name Bayanth symbolizes the gentle and calming influence of the wind, bringing renewal and vitality. It is a name that conveys the idea of constant movement and change, reflecting the dynamic nature of life.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions a Yaksha named Bayantha, who is a guardian of the forest and has the power to cause droughts. He is known to have been a friend of the Pandava prince, Bhima.

The Jain scripture, Harivamsha, describes a king named Bayadha or Bayanth, who ruled over Vidarbha during the reign of King Mahasen. He was a patron of the Jain monk, Haritaka, and helped in the construction of the Jain shrine at Dhank.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Bayanth is derived from Hindu mythology, specifically from the Mahabharata where Bayanth is a warrior in the great battle of Kurukshetra. Lastly, on YouTube, there are cosplay videos featuring Bayanth, demonstrating the character's enduring appeal and influence on popular culture.
